title: Lexeme timing reconciler and cache-impact attribution
creator: Priya Sharma
description:
Goal: provide deterministic per-lexeme timing and cache-hit attribution that can be joined to billing and latency dashboards without exploding event cardinality. We need an instrumentation approach that ties lexeme emit timings (microsecond resolution), KV-cache hit/miss annotations, and path metadata (model variant, kernel path, batch id) into a compact event stream and sampled traces. This ticket scopes the schema, sampling policy, minimal runtime hooks, and a rollout plan for the first internal customers (console queries, hosted text-gen routes).

Motivation: current per-request metrics obscure per-lexeme cost drivers. Engineering and product teams report regressions where a small portion of lexemes causes disproportionate latency and unit cost. The solution must: 1) avoid huge metrics cardinality by using aggregation keys and controlled sampling, 2) preserve exact accounting for cache hits vs misses, and 3) be joinable to existing traces to enable root-cause analysis across the serving layers.

Non-goals: this ticket does not change billing logic, alter public billing APIs, or add per-token charges in the console. It only produces telemetry that will be used to inform future cost models and dashboards.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime emits a compact lexeme_timing event for every request when sampling=full and for sampled requests otherwise; event fields documented in schema doc.
Each event includes lexeme_index, elapsed_us, cache_status (HIT/MISS/STALE), model_variant, kernel_path, batch_size, request_id; maximum event size kept under 1KB.
A sampled trace contains linked lexeme timing spans that appear in tracing UI with correlation to request-level span.
Aggregation job produces daily rollups that show latency and cost delta attributed to cache hits vs misses per model_variant and route.
Dashboard panels (latency breakdown and cache-impact) are created in Grafana/Console and validate against synthetic workload within ±5% of ground truth measurements.
Feature gated rollout completed with ability to turn off at edge without server restart.
steps: Design schema for lexeme_timing event and span tags (telemetry doc link below). Keep field set minimal; propose idempotent event key for de-duplication.
Implement runtime hooks: emit before_emit (timestamp), after_emit (timestamp + token returned), attach cache_status from KV layer.
Add sampling selector: 0.5% global baseline + adaptive on-slo-violation to increase sampling on high-latency requests.
Implement compact binary encoding for internal logs and JSON shim for external pipelines.
Add server flag and feature-flag gating for rollout; include safe defaults (disabled for small customers).
Create aggregation job that ingests lexeme_timing events, joins with request metadata, and computes per-lexeme latency histograms and cache-hit ratios.
Author dashboard panels and describe alerting thresholds for sudden increases in lexeme-level misses or skew in lexeme latency distribution.
Run canary on internal tenants (console, infra-test app) and compare lexeme-level sums to request-level timers to validate accounting.
Collect feedback, iterate on sampling and fields, then expand rollout.
comments: 2026-02-13 - Priya Sharma: Kickoff doc posted. Initial schema proposal attached. Decided to use 'lexeme' nomenclature internally to avoid confusion with user-facing 'token' billing language.

2026-02-20 - Marco Diaz: Implemented tracer hook and early emit events in staging runtime. Observed 0.7% CPU overhead at full sampling; using binary encoding reduces payload size by ~3x. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4387

2026-02-25 - Lina Park (SRE): KV layer added cache_status enum and returned hit provenance (local/remote/stale). Need to ensure propagation across async batch boundaries — planned fix in ENG-33120 dependency.
2026-03-03 - Data Eng (A. Chen): Aggregation job skeleton ready. Concern: high-cardinality model_variant+kernel_path combinations. Proposal: hash group into 'performance_bucket' to bound rollups.
2026-03-10 - Marco Diaz: Added adaptive sampling module. Tests show that under SLO violation sampling rises to 10% for affected requests enabling faster root cause detection.

2026-03-14 - Priya Sharma: Dashboard PR created for console: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/2271. Validation plan: run synthetic batch with deterministic cache hits and compare rollup outputs; target ±5% accuracy.
